scope: Faster answers to keys, voice commands and dictation. Thunderbird connects quickly when it was open first. Sound in Chrome no longer stays quiet on a headset.

topics.title: Response time record
details: Some keys or commands may still feel slow. Now Companion writes each slow one down.
The record is a file called response-times.txt in Companion's data folder.
It says which step was slow. It never keeps the words you say or type.
This helps us find and fix the slow spots.

topics.title: Faster keys and voice commands
details: Companion answers a key the moment you press it.
Short commands, such as next, check email and main menu, are acted on right away.
Before, every command went through the dictation engine a second time. That could add a second or more.

topics.title: Faster dictation
details: Only the part of the recording with your words goes to the dictation engine.
The quiet before and after you speak is left out, so your text comes back sooner.
Silence alone is no longer sent to the engine. This keeps the computer quicker while the microphone is on.

topics.title: Thunderbird opened first
details: Did you open Thunderbird first? Now email connects in a few seconds.
Before, it could take many minutes.
If Thunderbird still does not connect, Companion restarts it once, the normal way.
Thunderbird asks first if you are writing a message, so nothing is lost.

topics.title: Sound on headsets
details: Companion lowers other sound while it talks, then puts it back.
On some headsets, such as the Jabra Engage, sound in Chrome could stay quiet afterward.
Now it always comes back, on the headset and on your speakers.
If you set a level yourself in the volume mixer, Companion keeps it.
